Advances: ancora.gate

Severity: Medium (calibrated). Consolidated findings F14, F49, F53, F54, F55, F56, F57, F58, F65. Cannot have landed on the shipped branch: these are test-quality changes on code that already merged, and several need new fixtures.

The theme: several tests pass for reasons orthogonal to what they claim, and the two guards that enforce ancora architectural charter are vacuous if their matchers ever break.

F14 (the important one) — both static charter guards are of the form assert offenders == [] with NO positive control, so they would stay green forever if their AST matchers stopped matching. forbidden_spawner_test also resolves its root at runtime, so a file glob that matches nothing passes silently. Fix: pin the root at compile time with a module attribute, add a non-empty floor to both guards so an empty candidate set fails, and give each detector a positive control asserting it fires on a known offender before the allowlist excludes it.
F65 — related and worth doing in the same pass: the no-execution guarantee rests on all eight mix tasks declaring the deps.loadpaths requirement, which keeps the target build off the code path, and NOTHING tests that. Changing one task to compile would weaken the charter with no failing test. Add a static test asserting every mix task declares exactly that requirement, in the style of the existing guards.
F49 — scope the exactly-eight-tasks comparison to Application.spec(:ancora, :modules) so the no-task-under-any-other-name clause is actually asserted.
F54 — replace the is_function/2 tautology with Code.ensure_loaded!/1 plus function_exported?/3, matching the three siblings in the same directory. As written it passes with the function deleted.
F55 — anchor the review grouping assertions with the String.split technique the same file already uses at line 112, or rename the test to what it actually covers: today it asserts on a hand-built view model rather than the grouping code.
F56 — give spec_next_test a fixture project and --root, and assert a specific classification rather than whatever the working tree happens to hold.
F57 — add test/ancora_test.exs covering Ancora.validate/2 directly: one warning-level finding, fail false without strict and fail true with it, plus the checked counts. It has an external caller and no direct test.
F53 — assert growth and shrink suppression under acknowledgment, and the never-raise guard, under the ancora.gate.acknowledgment_clears tag.
F58 — delete the six dead moduletag tmp_dir lines.

Deliberately dropped by the review, do not relitigate: a style sweep over assertion failure messages that do not name what broke, with no defect behind it.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/static/forbidden_spawner_test.exs and forbidden_writer_test.exs (positive controls, compile-time root, non-empty floor), a new static test asserting every mix task declares the deps.loadpaths requirement (tagged to the no-execution requirement in ancora.gate or ancora.tasks), test/ancora/static/exactly_eight_test.exs scoped to Application.spec(:ancora, :modules), the is_function/2 tautology replaced, test/ancora/review_test.exs grouping assertions anchored, test/mix/tasks/spec_next_test.exs on a fixture with --root, a new test/ancora_test.exs for Ancora.validate/2, growth/shrink suppression and never-raise under ancora.gate.acknowledgment_clears, six dead moduletag tmp_dir lines deleted
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) each charter guard fails when its allowlist is emptied against a known offender and fails when the candidate set is empty (prove both in the IMPLEMENTED comment by temporarily breaking the matcher and showing the red run); (2) changing one mix task's requirement away from deps.loadpaths makes a test fail; (3) the exactly-eight test asserts no task exists under any other name; (4) the review grouping test exercises the grouping code, not a hand-built view model; (5) spec_next asserts a specific classification on a fixture; (6) Ancora.validate/2 has direct coverage of strict and non-strict verdicts and counts
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: each charter guard fails on a known offender and on an empty candidate set, and every mix task provably declares deps.loadpaths.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- test/** (this is a test-only ticket)
- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md (tag, scenario, and verification-block edits only)

- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base <your base>` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator after the fifth admission defect of this epic. Derivation is file-scoped: every production function called anywhere in a test file joins every subject tagged anywhere in that file, and siblings merging into the epic tip change that set under you, so no list written at admission stays correct. Rule: acknowledgment edits only. Write one substantive requirement or scenario statement describing what THIS ticket changed as THAT subject observes it, verified by execution that the named input actually reaches that subject. Never restate another subject's contract in a second home, never weaken a must, never delete a requirement, never use a Spec-Ack trailer for it. If the subject genuinely observes no change from your work, say so in your completion record and stop; that is an escalation to the orchestrator, not a failure. Every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; an affects: entry on your own ADR is the expected form.)
- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

- .spec/decisions/** (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator, third instance of the same admission defect, this one found by the ancora-xla.4 verifier. Ancora.PolicyFiles.missing_decision?/1 at lib/ancora/policy_files.ex:115 fires change/missing_decision whenever any path under .spec/specs/ changes without an accompanying decision-record change in the SAME diff. Every ticket here is required to edit a spec, so this finding is structurally guaranteed and the decision-record edit is forced rather than optional. Write a real contract statement describing what you actually built; do NOT add a hollow line to silence the finding, which a grader will read as finding-silencing and bounce.)

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/** (read-only; if a new test exposes a real production defect, comment it on this ticket and file a child under ancora-xla instead of fixing it here)
- priv/**
- docs/**

Out of Scope (intent):
- no assertion-message style sweep (dropped by the review)
- no merging of the two git fixture helpers (dropped by the review)
- assertional test edits here are the point; expect the critical grader path

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket


SCOPE ADDITION (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 21:05), from the ancora-xla.2 Elixir test critic. This ticket's subject is giving thin tests real teeth, and these are four conditional clauses with no test at all, on surfaces ancora-xla.2 created or touched.

1. lib/ancora/derive.ex:125. The `catch kind, reason -> {:error, {:resolver_throw, ...}}` sibling of the rescue clause that IS tested. A closure that throws rather than raises closes it.
2. lib/ancora/gate.ex:423 and the :cat_file_batch_timeout arm of run_context_error/1 at :408. Both untested. This matters beyond coverage arithmetic: ancora-xla.2's behaviour item (4) claims it "maps EVERY RunContext.start/3 failure to {:env, message}", and that claim is currently proved for one atom out of three.
3. lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex:71, the `rescue ArgumentError -> close(port); {:error, :port_poisoned}` path. The new poisoning test does not reach it, because it returns earlier at the Port.info == nil guard on :50.
4. lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex:31, open/1 returning :git_executable_not_found. Untested; the existing PATH-rewrite test covers Git.run/2 only.

Two smaller items from the same review, both in test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs and both about the unreadable-input test ancora-xla.2 added:
- :80 asserts `result.stdout =~ relative`, which pins that the diagnostic names the file but not why it failed. Adding the permission-denied text or the remedy string would stop an unrelated future environment failure that happens to mention the path from satisfying this assertion.
- :74-87 runs two subprocess cases inside one `for`, so the lib/ case never runs if the test/ case fails and one bug hides the other. Two named tests give independent signal.

Also noted and NOT assigned anywhere, because it is genuinely fine: close/1's bounded wait at batch_port.ex:100-116 has no direct test, but ancora-xla.2 correctly reverted the vacuous 10 millisecond exit-status receive back to a port monitor with a 500 millisecond bound, and three independent measurements confirmed the revert. Coverage there would be nice rather than necessary.

Add whichever of the above your Allowed touches already cover; the four conditional clauses are the ones that matter, since they close a claim this epic has already shipped once as overstated.

BLOCKING 1 - test/ancora/git_batch_port_test.exs:141-148, "fetch converts a Port.command error into a closed poisoned port". The test stringifies the compiled clauses of BatchPort.fetch/3 and asserts four substrings are present. It proves those four substrings appear somewhere in fetch/3. It does not prove the rescue clause does anything, because every substring is satisfied by code outside the rescue. `{:error, :port_poisoned}` is already in the `Port.info(port) == nil` early return at lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex:50. `{:close` is already in the `{:error, _reason} -> close(port); error` branch at :61-63. `rescue` and `[ArgumentError]` survive any rescue body at all. Vacuous-again mutation: rewrite lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex:68-70 to `rescue ArgumentError -> :ok` and all four assertions still pass, with the port left open and the caller getting `:ok` instead of an error. The test is green while the named behaviour is gone. This is the scope-addition item 3 clause and it is still untested. A deterministic seam does exist and is worth trying before falling back to inspection: `:erlang.port_command/2` raises badarg from a process that is not the port's connected process, so `BatchPort.open(root)` in the test process followed by `Task.async(fn -> BatchPort.fetch(batch, "HEAD:file") end) |> Task.await()` should reach the rescue with the port alive, letting you assert `{:error, :port_poisoned}` and `Port.info(port) == nil` afterwards. If that turns out not to hold, the honest outcome is to say the clause is only reachable under a race and escalate, not to assert on source text.

BLOCKING 2 - test/ancora/gate_test.exs:50-61, "the gate maps batch timeout and poisoned-port failures to environment messages". Two halves, and the weak half is the one the test is named for. Lines 51-55 read the compiled clause bodies of the private Gate.run_context_error/1 and evaluate them, so they genuinely pin the two message strings and fail if either clause is deleted or rewritten with a guard. That part is acceptable as a message-text guard. Lines 57-60 are the part that carries the claim, and they are three substring matches over the concatenated text of all four clauses of Gate.gate_error/1, so nothing forces them to be satisfied by the same clause. `{:env, {:run_context_error` is contributed by the `{:cat_file_batch_exited, _status}` clause at lib/ancora/gate.ex:464-466 independently of the clause under test. Vacuous-again mutation: delete the guard clause at lib/ancora/gate.ex:459-462 and replace it with `defp gate_error(reason) when reason in [:cat_file_batch_timeout, :port_poisoned], do: raise("boom")`. Both atoms are still in the text, `{:env, {:run_context_error` is still in the text from the exited clause, all three assertions pass, and the gate now crashes on exactly the two failures the test says it maps. A clause reorder does the same. Beyond the mutation, the test proves nothing about any caller reaching the mapping, which is the specific overstatement the scope addition says this epic already shipped once. On reachability I confirmed the implementer's difficulty is real for one atom and not the other: Gate.run_after_preflight/2 at :66 calls RunContext.start/2, whose only failure is BatchPort.open returning `:git_executable_not_found`, so the timeout and poisoned atoms cannot arrive there at all. They arrive at gate_error/1 from the assembly path at :104 and :107, which does fetch through the port, so a Gate.check against a TmpGitRepo whose batch port has been poisoned mid-run is the shape that would exercise it. If no seam reaches it with lib/ read-only, drop the source-text assertions, keep 51-55, rename the test to what it covers, and file the gap as a child of ancora-xla rather than shipping a test whose name asserts the mapping.

BLOCKING 3 - test/ancora/static/exactly_eight_test.exs:6-26 and :28-38. Behavior item (3) of this ticket says the exactly-eight test asserts no task exists under any other name, and .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md:36 states "No task under any other name shall exist." Neither test asserts it. The first filters `Application.spec(:ancora, :modules)` down to task names that already start with "spec." before comparing, so anything not so named is discarded before the assertion. The second filters on the `Elixir.Mix.Tasks.Spec.` module prefix, so it is blind in the same direction. Vacuous-again mutation, which is really a never-was: add lib/mix/tasks/ancora.doctor.ex defining `Mix.Tasks.Ancora.Doctor`. `Mix.Task.task_name/1` yields "ancora.doctor", the "spec." filter drops it, the module-prefix filter drops it, both tests stay green, and the package now ships nine tasks against a must-priority requirement that it ship eight. The F49 instruction to scope to `Application.spec(:ancora, :modules)` was followed to the letter and it did fix the real problem of dependency tasks polluting the list, but the clause the ticket names is still unasserted. Filtering on the `Elixir.Mix.Tasks.` prefix instead of the "spec." task-name prefix, then comparing the resulting task names to the eight, closes it in one line.

Area 1, the two charter guards, holds and is the strongest work in the diff. Both roots are now compile-time module attributes built from `__DIR__` (forbidden_spawner_test.exs:4, forbidden_writer_test.exs:6), so they are absolute and cwd-independent; the previous `Path.expand("lib")` in the spawner would have globbed nothing from any other cwd and passed. Both have a non-empty floor (`assert candidates != []` at spawner :18 and writer :16) that fires before any detection, so a glob matching nothing is now red. Both prove the detector before filtering: spawner :20-22 asserts some detection lands inside lib/ancora/git.ex or lib/ancora/git/, writer :18-21 asserts some detection lands inside lib/ancora/output.ex or lib/ancora/output/, and each fails first if the matcher returns nothing for everything. The offenders they catch are a System.cmd, System.shell, Port.open or :os.cmd call added outside the git layer, and an IO.puts, IO.write, IO.inspect, Mix.shell or Mix.Shell.IO call added outside Output. One residual weakness, non-blocking: each positive control is satisfied by a single hit anywhere in the allowed layer, so it is coarse per detector kind rather than per kind. Breaking only the `Port.open` arm of the spawner walker leaves the control green on the `System.cmd` in lib/ancora/git.ex while a new Port.open elsewhere goes unseen; breaking only the `Mix.shell` arm of the writer walker leaves the control green on Output's IO.puts. A per-kind control, asserting each detected kind you rely on is present at least once in the allowed layer, would close that. Also minor: the writer's parse-error branch at :55 emits a detection tuple, so a syntax error in a file under lib/ancora/output/ would satisfy the positive control without any real detection.

Area 2, exactly_eight_test.exs:28-38, does prove deps.loadpaths rather than compile, and I checked the mechanism. `use Mix.Task` registers `@requirements` as an accumulating attribute, so `__info__(:attributes)[:requirements]` returns the declared list; the assertion compares that per-module list against the constant `["deps.loadpaths"]` for every module, so it is not the self-comparison its shape suggests. Swapping one task is caught: changing lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex:4 to `@requirements ["compile"]` makes the left list hold `["compile"]` for that module and the assertion fails, and the implementer reports having run exactly that mutation. Adding a second requirement is also caught, since accumulation yields a two-element list. Losing the app entirely is caught loudly rather than vacuously, because `Application.spec(:ancora, :modules)` returning nil raises on `Enum.filter`. The `length(spec_tasks) == 8` line is a real floor against a task being dropped. My only complaint about this test is the one in blocking finding 3, which is about what it does not look at rather than what it asserts.

Area 3 is covered by blocking findings 1 and 2. Summarising the verdict asked for: the run_context_error half of the gate test is a legitimate, if awkward, static message guard because it evaluates the clause body and fails when the clause moves or disappears; the gate_error half and the whole of the batch-port test are implementation-detail assertions dressed as behaviour tests, and both carry test names that state behaviour the assertions cannot see. The ticket's remit for static guards is the charter guards over lib/, not the internals of two private error mappings, so these do not inherit that licence.

Area 4 holds and is real execution throughout. spec_check_test.exs:65-78 now runs two independently named tests, each creating its own fixture, chmodding one real file to 0o000 and invoking the real task through run_mix_subprocess; the shared helper at :414-428 asserts status 1, that stdout names the relative path, that stdout carries `:file.format_error(:eacces)` so an unrelated environment failure that merely mentions the path no longer satisfies it, that the last stdout line is exactly the env verdict, and that stderr carries no RuntimeError. Splitting the old `for` means the lib/ case no longer hides behind the test/ case. The on_exit chmod restore is registered after the case's root cleanup, so LIFO restores permissions first, which is correct. gate_test.exs:441-462 runs against a real git repo with a real config lowering derived/drift to info, commits a real `Spec-Ack: derived/drift=warning` trailer, and asserts through Gate.check that the finding survives at `severity: :info` with `severity_source: :config` and that report.fail stays false, so the offender is a trailer that raises a configured severity and the test would fail if the trailer were honoured. Three other new tests are also honest execution: pipeline_test.exs:183-204 drives Derive.run with a membership resolver that throws and asserts `{:error, {:resolver_throw, path, :throw, :resolver_threw}}` plus caller survival, closing scope-addition item 1; git_batch_port_test.exs:129-139 empties PATH and asserts `{:error, :git_executable_not_found}` from the real BatchPort.open, closing item 4; ancora_test.exs gives Ancora.validate/2 its first direct test with exact checked counts and both strict and non-strict verdicts. spec_next_test.exs:7-31 now builds its own committed fixture and asserts `classification=uncovered frontier change`, `reconciliation=needs new subject` and the changed-file list, which is a specific classification rather than whatever the tree held; note it reaches the task via `mix run -e` and File.cd! rather than the `--root` flag the ticket named, so Mix task dispatch for spec.next is now only covered by the sibling tests in the same file, which is acceptable but worth knowing.

No deleted coverage and no weakened assertions elsewhere. The six `@moduletag :tmp_dir` removals are safe: nothing in the suite reads a `tmp_dir` context key, and Ancora.TestCase builds its own unique root in setup. The two async flips are corrections, not regressions. gate_test.exs:4 moves to async: false while the module has been installing VM-global `:erlang.trace_pattern` at :222, :261, :314 and :340 all along, and git_batch_port_test.exs:4 moves to async: false because the new test mutates PATH with System.put_env; ExUnit runs sync modules serially after the async ones, so neither global now leaks into a concurrent module. review_test.exs:80-101 is a genuine strengthening: splitting the HTML on the three section headers and adding `refute watched_interface =~ "Billing.void/2"` turns a set of bare substring checks into placement assertions, and while the view model there is still hand-built, four pre-existing production-builder tests in the same file at :121, :157, :172 and :199 cover the real grouping code, so F55's concern is answered. The is_function/2 tautology at spec_check_test.exs:255-261 is properly replaced with Code.ensure_loaded!/1 plus function_exported?/3 and would now fail if either run/1 were deleted. One cosmetic nit: git_batch_port_test.exs:130 is named "open returns data when git is absent from PATH" but asserts an error tuple.

- Intent-level scope concerns: none. mix.exs and mix.lock untouched, no new deps, no assertion-message style sweep, the two git fixture helpers were not merged.
- Targeted verification: the 14 diff-modified test files plus test/ancora/static/ ran green, 91 tests 0 failures. mix spec.check --base c330458 ends result=pass.
- Whitelist adherence: change-scoped + diff-touched tests + spec gate only; compile/format/credo/deps re-establishment: not run.
- Corpus-scoped claims: n/a — code diff. The two .spec/ files were checked claim by claim against execution; results in Notes.
- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)
- Audit-expanded scope: none, this is the first verification.

Mutation measurements (all in a disposable copy under the scratchpad, never in the stage worktree):
- forbidden_spawner, empty candidate set (@lib pointed at a nonexistent dir): FAILS at "assert candidates != []", line 17. Correct.
- forbidden_spawner, detector returns nothing (file_spawn_calls/1 stubbed to []): FAILS at the positive control, "spawn detector did not find the known subprocess call in Ancora.Git", line 21. Correct.
- forbidden_writer, empty candidate set: FAILS at "assert candidates != []", line 16. Correct.
- forbidden_writer, detector returns nothing (file_violations/1 stubbed to []): FAILS at "stdout detector did not find the known writer in Ancora.Output", line 20. Correct.
- deps.loadpaths guard, Mix.Tasks.Spec.Check switched to @requirements ["compile"]: FAILS at exactly_eight_test.exs:36 with the diff naming Check. Correct.
- Ninth spec.* task added (Mix.Tasks.Spec.Sneaky): BOTH exactly_eight tests fail. Correct.
- Ninth task under another name added (Mix.Tasks.Ancora.Sneaky, @requirements ["compile"]): BOTH exactly_eight tests stay GREEN. Gap 3.
- run_context_error/1 dead-coded (an earlier catch-all clause returning "shadowed" inserted above all three atom clauses): gate_test.exs:50 stays green, and the whole file stays green at 25 tests 0 failures. Gap 1.
- gate_error/1 guard list with :port_poisoned removed: gate_test.exs:50 FAILS at "gate_error_source =~ \":port_poisoned\"". So that one mutation is caught.
- BatchPort.fetch/3 rescue clause gutted (close(port) deleted, {:error, :port_poisoned} replaced with {:error, :rescue_is_now_broken}): git_batch_port_test.exs stays green at 8 tests 0 failures. Gap 2.
- Reachability probe for the rescue at batch_port.ex:71: opening the port from a non-owner process keeps Port.info/1 non-nil, but Port.command/2 does not raise ArgumentError from a non-owner on OTP 27. The fetch returns {:error, :cat_file_batch_timeout} instead. No deterministic route to that clause through the public API was found.

Verdict: FAIL

Gaps:
- ancora.gate.preflight_hard_fails, batch-timeout and poisoned-port arm: the test at gate_test.exs:50 is named "the gate maps batch timeout and poisoned-port failures to environment messages" and never calls the gate. It reads Gate's compiled debug_info, evaluates the private run_context_error/1 clause bodies, and substring-matches an inspected AST of gate_error/1. Measured: shadowing all three atom clauses with an earlier catch-all leaves it and the entire gate_test.exs file green, so the clauses can be dead code and nothing notices. The requirement's defining sentence is that these conditions make "mix spec.check exit non-zero with verdict result=fail tier=env and a message naming the remedy"; the test asserts no exit code, no tier, and no verdict line. The loosening it cannot catch is exactly the one a refactor produces: a new clause above the specific ones. Separately, run_context_error/1 as called from gate.ex:75 can never receive :cat_file_batch_timeout or :port_poisoned, because RunContext.start/3's only failure comes from BatchPort.open/1 and that returns only :git_executable_not_found. Those two atoms reach the env arm through gate_error/1 at gate.ex:104 and :107 instead. If the two atoms are genuinely unreachable end to end from Gate.check/2 with no injection seam, the ticket's own rule applies: say so in the completion record and escalate, rather than ship a green test whose name asserts the behaviour.
- Behaviour item on batch_port.ex:71: the test at git_batch_port_test.exs:141, "fetch converts a Port.command error into a closed poisoned port", is four substring assertions on an inspected AST and proves nothing about behaviour. Two of the four cannot fail from a rescue-clause change at all: "{:close" is satisfied by the close(port) call in the collect_one error arm at batch_port.ex:61, and "{:error, :port_poisoned}" is satisfied by the Port.info guard's return at batch_port.ex:50. Measured: deleting close(port) from the rescue and changing its return atom leaves all 8 tests in the file green. I also measured that the clause has no deterministic seam (see the reachability probe above), so this is the same escalation case as Gap 1, not a test that needs a slightly better assertion.
- Behaviour to demonstrate (3), "the exactly-eight test asserts no task exists under any other name": not delivered. ancora.tasks.exactly_eight states "No task under any other name shall exist." Both tests in exactly_eight_test.exs scope to Application.spec(:ancora, :modules), which was F49's ask, then discard everything that is not named spec.* — the first via String.starts_with?(&1, "spec."), the second via the "Elixir.Mix.Tasks.Spec." prefix. That filter throws away precisely the tasks the second sentence is about. Measured: a real ninth Mix task in the package under another name, declaring @requirements ["compile"], leaves both tests green. The same hole means the new deps.loadpaths guard does not constrain a package task outside the Spec namespace either.

Notes:
- Behaviour item (4), "the review grouping test exercises the grouping code, not a hand-built view model", is literally unmet: review_test.exs:79 still feeds the hand-built map from view/2 into Html.render/1. I am not counting it as a Gap. F55 offered anchoring with String.split as an acceptable alternative and that is what was built, the section-scoped assertions plus "refute watched_interface =~ Billing.void/2" are a real strengthening, and the grouping code itself is separately driven through Review.build/2 by the sibling tests at review_test.exs:161, :176 and :204 under the same tag.
- spec_next_test uses File.cd! inside a mix run -e script rather than --root, because mix spec.next has no --root flag. The classification assertion is fixture-specific ("changed_files:\n- README.md"), so the fixture is real. Worth knowing that the Mix project loaded in that subprocess is ancora's, not the fixture's.
- The two messages the new gate scenario codifies, "git cat-file batch timed out" and "git cat-file batch port is unusable", name no remedy, while ancora.gate.preflight_hard_fails requires "a message naming the remedy" and the sibling git-executable message does supply one. The messages predate this ticket and live in lib/, so fixing them is out of scope here, but the ticket has now written them into a scenario.
- ancora.gate.scenario.batch_failures_are_environment_errors is the one added spec sentence not backed by execution. Its "then" clause "both mappings return through the environment-error arm rather than raising" rests on a substring match against an inspected AST term, not on a run. Every other added sentence I checked is true by execution: the git-absent scenario's "{:error, :git_executable_not_found} as data", the mix_tasks_load_only_dependencies scenario including "changing one task to a compiling requirement fails the test", the forbidden_spawner scenario's non-empty rooted candidate list and pre-allowlist positive control, the drift/growth/shrink and trailer-never-raises scenarios, and the strict_verdict scenario's Ancora.validate/2 counts. The decision-record edit is accurate as written.
- gate_test.exs moved from async: true to async: false and git_batch_port_test.exs from async: true to async: false. The batch-port change is justified by the PATH mutation in the new test. The gate_test change is unexplained and serializes 25 tests, which measured 4.7s sync on its own.

title: Give the static guards and thin tests real teeth
